outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no source I found settles, bounds or moves the count of supersingular primes below X for any non-CM elliptic curve over Q; the post-freeze work is averages over genus-2 families, upper bounds for abelian surfaces and higher-dimensional varieties, a fixed-Frobenius-field lower bound, and a conditional pair-of-curves statement, none of which is the bullet's quantity, and no AI system is credited with any of it.
problem_asks: The bullet, Wikipedia 26 Jan 2024 wording: 'Lang and Trotter's conjecture on supersingular primes that the number of supersingular primes less than a constant X is within a constant multiple of √X/ln X'. Parts: (1) an upper bound: for some constant C and all large X, the number of supersingular primes p < X is at most C·√X/log X; (2) a lower bound: for some constant c > 0 and all large X, the count is at least c·√X/log X. 'Within a constant multiple' asks for both. Not stated in the bullet but needed to read it: the object the primes belong to. The literature (Lang and Trotter 1976, as reported by the Wikipedia article 'Supersingular prime (algebraic number theory)') takes a non-CM elliptic curve E over Q and counts primes p < X with a_p(E) = 0, and states the asymptotic π_{E,0}(X) ~ C_E·√X/log X with C_E > 0 depending on E. That asymptotic implies both halves of the bullet. The bullet names no curve, no family, and no dependence of the constant on E. Reading note: for CM curves Deuring's theorem gives a count of about X/(2 log X), so the √X scale is a non-CM statement; the bullet does not exclude CM curves.

events.what_happened: Chihiro Ando and Shushi Harashita (Yokohama National University), arXiv:2604.00822, 'The Lang-Trotter conjecture on average for genus-2 curves with S3 reduced automorphism group'. Extends the Lang-Trotter conjecture to genus-2 curves and proves an average analogue over the family C_λ: y² = x(x−1)(x−λ)(x−(λ−1)/λ)(x−1/(1−λ)), averaging over integers λ with |λ| ≤ N and N > X^{1+ε}. Theorem B: the average of φ_λ(X) is asymptotic to (6+4√3)π/9 · √X/log X. Theorem C: a rational-λ version with constant 4(3+2√3)/(3π). The paper makes no statement about any single λ. The abstract describes the elliptic-curve Lang-Trotter conjecture on average as established by Fouvry and Murty and calls the single-curve conjecture open.
events.revisions: v1 1 Apr 2026; v2 revised 9 Oct 2026 (content of v2 not read). The abstract page's comments say part of v1 was moved to a companion paper, 'On the reduction modulo p of the Hilbert class polynomial of discriminant -3p' (companion not located).
events.delivers: For the genus-2 family C_λ with S3 reduced automorphism group, an average over λ of the paper's counting function φ_λ(X) has the order √X/log X, with constant (6+4√3)π/9 (Theorem B), under N > X^{1+ε}. Averages over a parameter of genus-2 curves, not elliptic curves, and not individual curves. The exact definition of φ_λ was not confirmed from text I could read.
events.remains: Everything the bullet asks for about elliptic curves: the count for each non-CM elliptic curve over Q, both halves. Also the single-curve genus-2 case, which the paper does not treat.
events.direction: An average-only analogue on a genus-2 family. It has the conjectured order √X/log X and so points the same way as the bullet, but it bounds no elliptic curve's count and its averaging parameter is the family, not the prime.

events.what_happened: Tian Wang (MPIM Bonn), arXiv:2608.17639, 'Infinitely many primes with a fixed Frobenius field for an elliptic curve over Q' (MPIM-Bonn-2026 report). For certain families of non-CM elliptic curves E/Q and squarefree Δ (composite, Δ ≡ −1 mod 8, with j(E) an even integer and odd conductor primes of Kodaira type I0*), proves π_E(x, Q(√−Δ)) ≫ (log log x)^{1−ε}, so infinitely many primes have Frobenius field equal to that fixed imaginary quadratic field. Also gives power-saving upper bounds for a restricted count. The paper counts fixed Frobenius fields, not trace-zero primes; Elkies' supersingular infinitude is cited as background.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the abstract page.
events.delivers: A lower bound (log log x)^{1−ε} for the number of primes whose Frobenius field is the fixed field Q(√−Δ), for the stated families. This is a different quantity from the trace-zero count: for a supersingular prime p the Frobenius field is Q(√−p), which varies with p, so the fixed-field count does not count supersingular primes.
events.remains: The trace-zero count of the bullet for any curve, and its √X/log X order.
events.direction: Does not bear on the bullet's quantity. It is a lower bound for a different count, and it is far below √X/log X.

events.what_happened: Chihiro Ando, arXiv:2408.13695, 'The Lang-Trotter conjecture on average for genus-2 curves with Klein-4 reduced automorphism group'. Average analogue over C_λ: y² = x(x−1)(x+1)(x−λ)(x−1/λ), with λ over integers, |λ| ≤ N and N > X^{1+ε}. Theorem B: (1/N)·Σ φ_λ(X) ~ (3π/2)·√X/log X. Theorem C: a rational-λ version with constant 9/π. The introduction states the elliptic-curve Lang-Trotter count as open. The paper proves nothing about a single λ.
events.revisions: v1 25 Aug 2024; v2 29 Aug 2025 (content of v2 not read).
events.delivers: An average of φ_λ over a family of genus-2 curves with Klein-4 reduced automorphism group, of order √X/log X with constant 3π/2 (Theorem B). Average only.
events.remains: The single-curve elliptic count (the bullet), and the single-curve genus-2 count.
events.direction: Same as the 2026 genus-2 paper: an average-only analogue of the bullet's order on a family of genus-2 curves, not a bound on an elliptic curve.

events.what_happened: Tian Wang, arXiv:2402.12218, 'Distribution of supersingular primes for abelian surfaces'. For an absolutely simple abelian surface A over a number field K, gives unconditional upper bounds on the number of prime ideals of norm up to x at which A has supersingular reduction, in three cases by endomorphism algebra (trivial, real multiplication, quaternion multiplication). The MPIM Bonn talk page (17 Apr 2024) describes the same topic and recalls the Lang-Trotter conjecture for non-CM elliptic curves.
events.revisions: v1 19 Feb 2024. Later HTML versions v2 and v3 are linked from search results; their contents were not read. An MPIM preprint 2024-11 (archive.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/5060) appears in search results; its PDF could not be read, so whether it is this paper is not established.
events.delivers: Unconditional upper bounds on supersingular-prime counts for absolutely simple abelian surfaces over number fields. Not elliptic curves; no lower bound; the exponent and form of the bound were not read.
events.remains: The elliptic-curve count of the bullet, both halves.
events.direction: An upper-bound result in a higher-dimensional setting. It cuts neither for nor against the elliptic-curve bullet.

events.what_happened: Chun-Yin Hui, arXiv:2504.08088, 'On distribution of supersingular primes of abelian varieties and K3 surfaces'. For an abelian variety or K3 surface X over a number field K, proves the supersingular primes have density zero when X is non-CM, and gives asymptotic upper bounds for the counting function using an effective Chebotarev density theorem of Serre. The abstract was read; the body was not.
events.delivers: Density zero and upper bounds for supersingular-prime counts of non-CM abelian varieties and K3 surfaces. Not elliptic curves; no lower bound; no asymptotic order.
events.remains: The bullet entirely for elliptic curves.
events.direction: Upper-bound and density results for other objects. It cuts neither way on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Fangu Chen, arXiv:2511.06654, 'Infinitely many supersingular primes for some Mumford's abelian fourfolds'. Per a search snippet (submitted 10 Nov 2025), extends Elkies' infinitude theorem to certain families of abelian fourfolds parametrised by Shimura curves of Hodge type. Not opened; the snippet is the only source.
events.delivers: Infinitude of supersingular primes for certain abelian fourfolds. Existence only, not a count, and not elliptic curves.
events.direction: An infinitude result for another object. It cuts neither way on the bullet.

events.what_happened: arXiv:2504.13498, 'Supersingular primes and Bogomolov property' (April 2025). Per a search snippet and a review page, a conditional result: if a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field has infinitely many supersingular primes, a Bogomolov-type property holds for certain fields generated by torsion. Not opened; snippet and review page only.
events.delivers: A conditional statement that assumes infinitude of supersingular primes and concludes a Bogomolov-type property. It is not a count and does not use the √X/log X order.
events.direction: Conditional on a different statement (infinitude) and about a different property. It cuts neither way on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Christopher Daw and Georgios Papas, arXiv:2605.00759, 'Lang-Trotter phenomena and unlikely intersections' (v1 1 May 2026). Shows that the Lang-Trotter conjecture for pairs of elliptic curves implies new cases of the Zilber-Pink conjecture for curves in A_3, using André's G-functions method. The pair version is conditional on that conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 per the abstract page; other versions not checked.
events.delivers: Conditional on the pair version of Lang-Trotter (two curves, coincidence of supersingular or trace conditions), it yields Zilber-Pink cases for A_3. Nothing unconditional about the count for one curve.
events.remains: The bullet entirely. The pair version is a different conjecture.
events.direction: Conditional consequence of a different (pair) conjecture. It cuts neither way on the single-curve bullet.

events.what_happened: Michael Bennett and Samir Siksek, 'A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums' (arXiv:1709.01022, Sept 2017; Annals of Mathematics 191(2), 2020). A Diophantine result on products of consecutive terms in arithmetic progression being perfect powers; the proof uses results on supersingular primes for non-CM elliptic curves. This is a different problem that uses supersingular primes as a tool; it is not the bullet. The Lean-eval benchmark page for it (opened) states Theorem 2 with a sorry placeholder and does not mention Lang-Trotter.
events.revisions: not checked on arXiv; Annals publication 2020.
events.delivers: A result about perfect powers in arithmetic progressions, not about the count of supersingular primes. It uses the existence of supersingular primes for non-CM curves, not a count.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the paper
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (volume 191, issue 2, 2020), per the Annals listing seen in search

events.direction: Uses supersingular-prime results for a different purpose. Not a result about the bullet's count.

events.what_happened: Nathan Fugleberg and Nahid Walji, arXiv:2109.05661, 'On the distribution of traces of Frobenius for families of elliptic curves and the Lang-Trotter conjecture on average' (v1 13 Sep 2021). Distribution results for traces of Frobenius over several one-parameter families, including Lang-Trotter on average; the abstract describes generalisations and bounds of Sha-Shparlinski's average results.
events.revisions: v1 per the abstract page; other versions not checked.
events.delivers: Averaged Lang-Trotter-type results over families of elliptic curves. No single-curve result is claimed in the abstract.
events.remains: The single-curve count of the bullet.
events.direction: Average results over families, the same kind as the Fouvry-Murty average. They are consistent with the bullet's order but do not bound a single curve.

events.what_happened: Stephan Baier, arXiv:math/0609095, 'The Lang-Trotter Conjecture on Average' (v1 4 Sep 2006). For y² = x³ + ax + b with |a| ≤ A and |b| ≤ B, A, B > x^{1/2+ε} and AB > x^{3/2+ε}: the arithmetic mean of π_E^r(x), the count of primes p ≤ x with Frobenius trace r, is asymptotic to C_r·√x/log x. Says it improves a result of David and Pappalardi. The abstract was read.
events.revisions: v1 only per the abstract page.
events.delivers: An average asymptotic over a two-parameter family, for each trace r including r = 0 (supersingular). No single-curve result.
events.remains: The single-curve count of the bullet.
events.direction: Average asymptotic of the bullet's order. Consistent with the bullet, not a bound on one curve.

events.what_happened: Nahid Walji, 'Supersingular distribution on average for congruence classes of primes', Acta Arithmetica 142(4) (2010), 387-400, also her Caltech PhD thesis (submitted Dec 2010). Shows a congruence-class bias on average: on average twice as many supersingular primes are congruent to 2 mod 3 as to 1 mod 3 (per abstract). Reposted to arXiv as 1307.5346 on 19 Jul 2013 as 'a preprint of an old paper'. Date taken from the 2010 journal version per the first-public-argument rule.
events.revisions: arXiv 1307.5346 v1 19 Jul 2013 only; a repost of the 2010 paper.
events.delivers: An average result over a family of elliptic curves, showing a congruence-class bias for supersingular primes on average. No single-curve result claimed in the abstract.
events.remains: The single-curve count of the bullet, and the constant for an individual curve.
events.direction: An average result that points in the bullet's direction on average but says nothing about one curve's count.

events.what_happened: Min Sha and Igor Shparlinski, 'Lang-Trotter and Sato-Tate distributions in single and double parametric families of elliptic curves', Acta Arithmetica 170 (2015). Per search snippets only, gives Lang-Trotter averages over polynomially parametrised families, with parameters of bounded height. Not opened.
events.delivers: Averages over parametrised families of elliptic curves. No single-curve result per the snippet.
events.remains: The single-curve count of the bullet.
events.direction: Average-only results. Consistent with the bullet's order but not a single-curve bound.

events.what_happened: Etienne Fouvry and M. Ram Murty, 'On the Distribution of Supersingular Primes', Canadian Journal of Mathematics 48(1) (1996), 81-104. The CJM abstract excerpt, read on the Cambridge page, says: for a fixed elliptic curve E over Q, the number of primes p ≤ x with supersingular reduction mod p is greater than a bound (the bound is an image on the page and was not readable) for any positive δ and x sufficiently large; and 'we also establish several results related to the Lang-Trotter conjecture'. Secondary sources (Ando 2024/2026 and Walji) describe the average result over y² = x³ + ax + b with A, B > X^{1+ε} and asymptotic constant 4π/3 · √X/log X.
events.revisions: Cambridge page shows 'published online 20 November 2018' (archival). Not checked further.
events.delivers: Per the abstract excerpt, an unconditional lower bound for a fixed curve (exponent not readable), and an average Lang-Trotter result over a family (per secondary sources). The lower bound is not stated to be of order √X/log X, and I could not confirm its form.
events.remains: Whether the lower bound reaches the bullet's order for one curve; the upper half of the bullet for one curve.
events.direction: Its average result points in the bullet's direction. Its single-curve lower bound might point the same way, but I could not read its exponent, so I cannot say how it cuts against the bullet's lower half.

events.what_happened: C. David and F. Pappalardi, average distribution of Frobenius traces over families of elliptic curves, extended to any fixed trace r (per secondary descriptions in Baier's paper and in Walji's work). I did not find the primary paper. Date not established. Baier (2006) improved this result, so it predates 2006.
events.delivers: Per secondary descriptions only: an average Lang-Trotter-type result for each trace r over families. Not a single-curve result.
events.remains: The single-curve count of the bullet.
events.direction: Average-only. Consistent with the bullet's order, not a single-curve bound.

events.what_happened: Jean-Pierre Serre, Quelques applications du théorème de densité de Chebotarev (Publ. IHÉS, 1981), per secondary citations. Density zero of supersingular primes for non-CM curves (by Chebotarev applied to torsion-point fields), an unconditional upper bound π_{E,ss}(x) ≪ x(log x)^{−3/2+ε}, and a conditional bound π_{E,ss}(x) ≪ x^{3/4} under GRH (as stated in the Wikipedia article's text). The Wikipedia article gives 1968 as the year of the density-zero result; other sources give 1981. Not read in primary form.
events.delivers: Density zero for supersingular primes of non-CM curves; an unconditional upper bound well above √X/log X; a GRH upper bound of order x^{3/4}, which is also above the bullet's order.
events.remains: Both halves of the bullet, and the √X/log X order.
events.doubts: Sources disagree on the year of the density-zero result (1968 per the Wikipedia article's text; 1981 per other secondary sources) and attribute the x^{3/4} bound to Serre under GRH in one source and to Elkies (1991, unconditional) in another. The attribution is unresolved here; the primary text was not read.
events.direction: Upper bounds far above the conjectured order. They do not contradict the bullet and are weaker than it.

events.what_happened: D. Wan, 1990, improved the unconditional upper bound for the count of supersingular primes to π_{E,ss}(x) ≪ x(log x)^{−2+ε} by adding a sieve lemma. Attested in secondary sources (Elkies 1991 text as quoted in a search snippet; a 2024 abelian-surface paper's restatement). Primary text not read.
events.delivers: An unconditional upper bound x(log x)^{−2+ε}, well above √X/log X.
events.direction: An upper bound well above the conjectured order; it does not contradict the bullet.

events.what_happened: Noam Elkies, 1987: every elliptic curve over Q has infinitely many supersingular primes (proof via CM cycles and Deuring lifting). Extended in 1989 to elliptic curves over number fields with at least one real embedding. The journal citation (Invent. Math. 89, 1987) was not confirmed from a source I could read.
events.delivers: Infinitude of supersingular primes for each E/Q (and, from 1989, for number fields with a real embedding). No count and no order.
events.remains: The count and its order (both halves).
events.direction: Qualitative infinitude. It is consistent with the bullet but does not address its count.

events.what_happened: Noam Elkies, 'Astérisque' 198-200 (1991), p. 127 (Numdam item AST_1991__198-199-200__127_0). Per secondary descriptions: a probabilistic heuristic giving about √x/log x supersingular primes for non-CM E/Q (each prime is supersingular with probability about p^{−1/2}), and an upper bound π_{E,ss}(x) ≪ x^{3/4}. The primary PDF could not be read.
events.delivers: A heuristic count of order √x/log x (the conjectured order) and an upper bound of order x^{3/4}. No proof of the √x/log x order.
events.remains: The proof of both halves for any curve.
events.doubts: Sources disagree on whether the x^{3/4} bound is unconditional (one secondary source) or under GRH (another, matching Serre's GRH result). The primary text was not readable, so the attribution is unresolved.
events.direction: A heuristic supporting the bullet's order, and an upper bound above that order. It does not settle the bullet.

disputes.summary: Sources disagree on the year of Serre's density-zero result (1968 per the Wikipedia article's text; 1981 in other secondary sources) and on whether the x^{3/4} upper bound is unconditional (Elkies 1991 in one source) or conditional on GRH (Serre, in another). This is an attribution question about older results, not a priority dispute over the bullet.

summary: The bullet is on Wikipedia's list under Algebraic number theory, linked to 'Supersingular prime (algebraic number theory)'. I read the list page, that article, the abstract or HTML of every 2024-2026 preprint I found, the CJM 1996 page for Fouvry-Murty, and the MPIM talk page. The article states the literature form, π_{E,0}(X) ~ C_E·√X/log X for non-CM E/Q (Lang and Trotter 1976), and says 'As of 2026, this conjecture remains open'. I found no source that settles, bounds or moves the single-curve count for any non-CM elliptic curve since 26 Jan 2024. The post-freeze work is: averages over genus-2 families, Ando (arXiv 2408.13695, Aug 2024) and Ando-Harashita (arXiv 2604.00822, Apr 2026), both with the conjectured order on average; an upper-bound result for abelian surfaces, Wang (arXiv 2402.12218, Feb 2024); density and upper bounds for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces, Hui (arXiv 2504.08088, Apr 2025); an infinitude result for abelian fourfolds, Chen (arXiv 2511.06654, Nov 2025, snippet only); a conditional Bogomolov-type statement, arXiv 2504.13498 (snippet only); a fixed-Frobenius-field lower bound, Wang (arXiv 2608.17639, Aug 2026); and a conditional pair-of-curves consequence, Daw-Papas (arXiv 2605.00759, May 2026). Close calls: (a) the averages are the nearest events in kind, since they are asymptotics of the conjectured order, but each averages over a parameter of a family, so it bounds no single curve; I recorded them as analogues and left the weighing to the judging pass. (b) The bullet's two-sided wording does not name a curve, whereas the literature asymptotic does. (c) Fouvry-Murty (1996) claims an unconditional lower bound for a fixed curve, but the displayed bound is an image I could not read, so I cannot say whether it reaches the bullet's lower half. (d) The x^{3/4} attribution is unresolved (see disputes). AI: no source I read, and no search result, credits an AI system with any work on this problem. The AI searches (the problem name with AI terms, AI-prover and lab announcements such as AlphaProof Nexus and OpenAI's Erdős results, Lean and mathlib, AI counterexample trackers) turned up AI work on other problems only. The only Lean-related hit is the Bennett-Siksek Erdős benchmark, a human paper, whose Lean statement is a placeholder with sorry and is not about this bullet.
competing_reading: One could count the 2026 genus-2 average (Ando-Harashita) and the 2024 abelian-surface upper bounds (Wang) as movement on the bullet, reading 'supersingular primes' broadly and 'within a constant multiple' as a claim about averages or about any abelian-type object. I record them as analogues because the bullet's quantity is the count for elliptic curves, and the averages are over a family parameter. A second reading would take Fouvry-Murty 1996's single-curve lower bound as the bullet's lower half, if its exponent is √x/log x; I could not verify that, so that reading is open.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of arXiv 2604.00822 (v1 and v2) and 2408.13695: exact definition of φ_λ and whether any statement reaches a single curve. (2) Fouvry and Murty 1996, Theorem 1 or the lower-bound statement, to read the exponent. (3) Serre 1981 and Elkies 1991 primary texts, to settle the x^{3/4} and density-zero attributions. (4) Lang and Trotter 1976 (LNM 504), section 4, to see whether the conjecture is stated as an asymptotic or as the two-sided bound in the bullet. (5) A post-October-2026 check of arXiv math.NT for single-curve supersingular counts. (6) Opening arXiv 2608.05299 ('Elliptic matroids and modular curves'), whose AI-usage statement appeared in a search snippet, to check whether it touches supersingular counts.
